observations.summary: recordJobRun keeps a stored last_run_at that is up to 1 hour ahead of a new run, and jobsStatus ignores times ahead of now. After a clock running ahead writes a row, GET /api/status/jobs can show that job as never run or late for up to an hour. The result is a false alarm, not a missed one. Vercel clocks are NTP-synced, so this is not expected in practice.

observations.status: open (unconfirmed; not reproducible with real Twilio behaviour)
observations.summary: recordDelivery takes a per-request lock and recordSmsFailure takes the location lock. If a 'delivered' and an 'undelivered' receipt for the same SID arrived at the same moment, both could apply: the text would count as delivered and the request would also go by email. Twilio sends one final status per message, so this was not reproduced.

A 'delivered' receipt for a row that is no longer 'sent' (for example after a carrier failure), and every receipt for opt-out confirmations and owner emails, waits in pending_receipts until the daily purge. The rows hold IDs and status only.
